rules.rule: Do not rewrite the existing architecture unless explicitly approved.
Trace executable code before changing behavior; record documentation drift when prose conflicts with code.
Every audit factor must have a unique machine-readable ID in factor_registry.json.
Every factor must produce structured evidence before it is treated as reliable.
One factor failure must never fail a complete audit.
Never silently convert unknown factors into scored factors.
Never treat audit uncertainty as PASS.
N/A factors must not reduce the score.
ERROR and UNKNOWN must remain observable and must not silently become FAIL or PASS.
Audit evidence must come from the appropriate evidence provider.
Do not parse human-readable audit messages to recover numeric values.
Store structured factor values independently from display messages.
Represent crawl failures explicitly; never convert them into successful audit coverage.
Classifier errors must not automatically classify a website as REAL.
Frontend factor definitions must derive from the factor registry or a registry-backed API.
Validate database mappings against the factor registry.
Preserve existing API fields while introducing structured results; migrate consumers before removals.
Every audit-engine change requires automated verification and a factor-parity check.
